We need propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have three reactions: 1) amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine). 2) Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). 3) sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So retrosynthesis: target -> disconnect amide bond between C(=O)N and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So precursor1: aryl amine (aniline) c3ccccc3N and acid fragment: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2)cc1 (i.e., same molecule but with carboxylic acid instead of amide). Then second step: disconnect the α,β-unsaturated acid to aldehyde precursor and malonic acid? Actually Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. So precursor acid could be formed from aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) attached to sulfonamide? Wait the unsaturated acid is /C=C/C(=O)OH attached to aromatic ring c2ccc(... )cc2. So we can retrosynthetically break that to aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). So second precursor: aromatic aldehyde with sulfonamide attached: c2ccc(CHO)cc2 attached to NS(=O)(=O) to the other phenyl? Actually the sulfonamide is attached to the first phenyl ring (para to methyl). The sulfonyl group connects two phenyl rings: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2. So the sulfonamide formation step: we can disconnect sulfonyl chloride from amine. So precursor: amine (para-methyl aniline) Cc1ccc(N)cc1 and sulfonyl chloride: ClSO2-c2ccc(CHO)cc2 (or after Doebner step, the sulfonyl chloride attached to aromatic aldehyde). Actually after Doebner, we have sulfonyl attached to aromatic ring bearing the unsaturated acid. So we can think: step3 (forward) sulfonamide formation: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide. So retrosynthesis: target -> break sulfonamide to amine (para-methyl aniline) and sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2). Then step2: break unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid. So sulfonyl chloride precursor becomes ClSO2-c2ccc(CHO)cc2 after reverse Doebner? Actually Doebner gives unsaturated acid from aldehyde, not from sulfonyl chloride. The sulfonyl chloride is attached to aromatic ring; the unsaturated acid is attached to same ring via side chain. So we need to generate sulfonyl chloride with aldehyde, then Doebner to give unsaturated acid, then amide formation to give final amide.

Thus retrosynthetic tree:

Target (mol) -> Reaction1 (amide formation) -> precursors:
 A) amine: c3ccccc3N (aniline)
 B) acid sulfonamide: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2)cc1

Reaction2 (Doebner) applied to B (the acid sulfonamide) -> precursors:
 B1) sulfonyl chloride with aldehyde: ClSO2-c2ccc(CHO)cc2 (i.e., sulfonyl chloride attached to aromatic aldehyde)
 B2) malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH) (but may be implicit, not needed in route representation? Usually templates include malonic acid as reagent, but we can include as separate molecule.)

Reaction3 (sulfonamide formation) applied to B1 + amine (para-methyl aniline) -> B1 is sulfonyl chloride, amine is Cc1ccc(N)cc1.

Thus final route: three reactions.

We need template IDs for each step. We have template 401931 corresponds to amide formation (looks like amide from acid and amine with double bond). That matches step1.

We need template for Doebner modification. Search for functional_groups_broken: ["aldehydes"], formed: ["C-C double bonds", "carboxylic acid"] maybe. Let's search.
